opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Jesus is not rejecting Mary Magdalene. He is correcting the way she is trying to hold onto Him.

“Stop holding on to me” means something closer to: do not cling to me as though things are going back to the old way. He has risen, but He is not simply returning to ordinary earthly life. Everything has changed. Now He is moving toward the Ascension, and the relationship between Him and His followers will be lived in a new way through faith, the Spirit, and the life of the Church.

Then He says:

“I am going to my Father and your Father,
to my God and your God.”

That is stunning. He is bringing the disciples into His own relationship with the Father. Not by nature in the exact way He is the Son, but by adoption and grace. Because of His death and Resurrection, His Father becomes their Father. That is the whole victory opening up.

Then Mary “went and announced to the disciples.”

That matters too. She is sent. She cannot remain at His feet in that moment. Love must become witness. Encounter with the risen Christ leads to mission.

So the movement is:

Mary wants to cling.
Jesus tells her not to remain there.
He sends her outward.
She becomes the messenger of the Resurrection.

The passage is saying:
Do not try to keep Jesus only as a private comfort.
Receive Him as the risen Lord.
Then go tell the others.

In a very real sense, this is also our life. We want to hold onto God in the way that feels safe, familiar, and emotionally near. But Christ often says: do not cling to the old form. I am leading you into something deeper. Faith now must become trust, obedience, and witness.
